intro: Ship captains and mates operate complex vessels, watch conditions and make safety calls, skills that aviation and rail careers share. The closest of the 25 careers below is Commercial Pilots, with an 86% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $123,220, which is 33% more than the $92,460 water vessel officers earn.
why_it_works: Commanding a vessel means navigating, monitoring engines and weather, managing a crew and deciding fast when something changes. O*NET rates operation and control at 3.62 out of 5 for this job, and operations monitoring and judgment at 3.38. Aviation, rail and plant control rooms use the same skills. Most matches need no new degree. The gaps are operations analysis and systems evaluation.
tips: Commercial pilot training builds directly on your navigation and command experience.
Airline pilots earn $232,140, which is 151% more, but usually need a bachelor's degree and many flight hours.
Nuclear Technicians earn $110,240, or 19% more, and value strict monitoring routines.

faq.q: What jobs can former ship captains do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Commercial Pilots (86%), Locomotive Engineers (79%) and airline pilots, copilots and flight engineers (78%), based on O*NET 31.0. Gas Plant Operators are 72% matched and earn $87,820, which is 5% less than the $92,460 median for captains, mates and pilots.

faq.q: Which careers for ship captains pay more?
faq.a: 9 of the 25 matches pay more. Airline pilots earn $232,140 (151% more), Commercial Pilots $123,220 (33% more) and Nuclear Technicians $110,240 (19% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Airline flying usually needs a bachelor's degree and many logged hours.

faq.q: Do ship captains need more education to switch?
faq.a: Usually not. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than water vessel officers already have, including 9 of the top 10. A post-secondary certificate is common in the closest match, held by 36% of workers, though pilots need FAA licenses.

faq.q: What skills should ship captains learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations monitoring, operation and control, operations analysis and systems evaluation. Complex problem solving already rates 3.25 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so learning new control systems is the main step toward aviation or plant work.
